CharacterStyleRange.Content: Participant Wellbeing and Support

In FY25, RV continued to deliver essential programs and services to support industry participants and their families, including free 24/7 counselling service Stableline, the Thurgood Duckling Fund and Respectful Workplaces initiatives.

Additional training and education programs, including those funded by RV and delivered by the Australian Trainers Association (ATA) with support and engagement from RV’s Participant Wellbeing Manager, were also carried out.

The Participant Protection and Wellbeing team also launched its Wellbeing Muster initiative, which involves a presence at trackwork and jump-outs to ensure those at the heart of the industry are aware of the help and support that is available to them.
The facilities at RV’s headquarters continued to be used as emergency short-term accommodation for industry participants in the event of a serious racing related incident.

RV also delivered the second year of a subsidy to trainers for WorkCover costs and continued to invest into the ATA-managed WorkCover Support Services, which are in place to support injured stable staff and their employers once a workplace injury has occurred.

At the time of publication, RV has completed or commenced delivery of all agreed elements of the nine recommendations from the Office of the Racing Integrity Commissioner (ORIC) review into the industry’s victim support and complaint processes. This includes the launch of the Victorian Thoroughbred Racing Restorative Engagement Program in September 2025 following planning and development throughout FY25.

Administered by Alfi Health independently of RV, the voluntary and confidential Restorative Engagement Program was created to support individuals who have experienced historical sexual harassment, or sexual or physical assault while working in the VTRI prior to September 2023. Applications will be open for six months with the program to run for two years.
Health & Safety
RV has an unwavering commitment to promoting health and safety initiatives within the VTRI.

In FY25, RV engaged with the ATA to fund the delivery of pre-loss initiatives for the enhancement of safety in Victorian racing stables, including the provision of education programs on safety improvements for racing and training.

RV also continued to engage with industry participants, clubs and WorkSafe on improvements to safety via the Victorian Thoroughbred Racing Industry Safety Committee, and has worked collaboratively with CRV to advance health and safety at Victorian clubs, in particular those that offer training facilities.
Environment, Social and Governance Initiatives

Building a sustainable future for the VTRI remains of paramount importance to RV and is at the forefront of all major policy decisions. The identification, management, and reporting of Environment, Social and Governance (ESG) risks is essential to ensuring that RV focuses its efforts on elements that will make the most impact towards our sustainability. RV continues to review its ESG vulnerabilities and identify core areas of concern, with current focus areas including:
• Overseeing and managing capital projects with consideration for environmental consequences.
• Collaborating with clubs to encourage sustainable thinking in infrastructure, operational decisions and efficient utilisation of natural resources.
• Partnering with clubs and trainers to establish effective solutions for pollution and waste management.
• Creating pathways for individuals to thrive and grow within the industry.
• Advocating for diversity, equity, safety, and inclusion across the sector.
• Supporting industry investment to enable growth in related supply chains.
• Developing a robust strategy for managing industry risks and controls.
• Fostering a culture grounded in respect, accountability, and ethical decision-making.
• Implementing clear and efficient leadership and governance frameworks for the industry.
• Staying engaged and informed about relevant public policy and political developments.
Charitable Contributions
In addition to providing financial and social support to the VTRI, RV is pleased to have made worthy contributions to a number of charities and community groups throughout FY25.

The primary recipient was the Good Friday Appeal, which supports the Royal Children’s Hospital and their vital work for Australian families. RV was joined by CRV and Southside Racing in donating $140,000 to the 2025 appeal, taking RV and CRV’s contribution over the last seven years past $600,000.
RV has also made charitable contributions to Down Syndrome Victoria, RSL ANZAC Day Appeal, Fight MND, Kids First Australia and the Ballarat Foundation – United Way throughout FY25.

Beyond RV, metropolitan and country clubs have been significant contributors to the community utilising key events to raise funds for well-known charities and important causes within their local area.

Charity pins are an iconic part of the Spring Racing Carnival with the three metropolitan clubs collectively raising over $900,000 in 2024 for Ronald McDonald House Charities (VRC), Challenge – Children with Cancer (MRC) and Myeloma Australia (MVRC).

Other notable fundraisers included the MRC Foundation Gala in aid of Down Syndrome Victoria, MVRC’s Cheering for Charity initiative at night meetings and the VRC’s Melbourne Cup Tour National Sweep, which saw the Murrumburrah Harden Show Society pocket $50,000 as the community partner for Melbourne Cup winner Knight’s Choice.
